unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: Bayan Obo tailings. Two independent routes agree. (a) Tailings 6.55 Mt/a (2006) divided by Bayan Obo REO of about 57.8 kt (59% of China 98 kt, 2004; mismatched years) = 113 t tailings per t REO, times 1.0-1.6 Bq/g Th-232 = 1.1e8-1.8e8 Bq. (b) Ore 0.032% ThO2 (3566 Bq/g ThO2) at 5% REO and an assumed 15% overall REO recovery = 133 t ore per t REO = 1.5e8 Bq (100% recovery would be 2.3e7). Ra-228+ and Th-228+ in the tailings are assumed in equilibrium with the Th-232 head. The 15% recovery is an inference from route (a), not a sourced figure. Pre-1990 recovery and Fe-only operation unknown (iron concentrate Th was 0.024% early). Upper bound set to the derived 113 t x 1.6 Bq/g = 1.81e8 (earlier rounded 1.9e8).

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: Tailings U-238 0.022 Bq/g (S0404 Table 12, ref 74) x 113 t/t REO = 2.5e6. Low/high are a factor-2 judgement bound (one measurement).

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: Thorium in REE concentrate going to chemical processing: concentrate 5.3-10 Bq/g Th-232 (Table 12) at 50-70% REO; central 7.1 Bq/g at 60% REO. This Th ends mainly in RE slag (acid route gross alpha 80-200 Bq/g; stored at Baotou, 261 000 t cumulative 2006), partly in off-gas (about 770 Bq per t concentrate roasted in 2006, negligible) and in products (RE oxide 0.0069% ThO2 = 0.25 Bq/g). Equilibrium daughters Ra-228+ and Th-228+ assumed equal to the head.

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: Thorium left in REE oxide products (0.0069% ThO2 = 0.246 Bq/g): about 2.5e5 Bq/t REO. Counted as embedded in products, not a residue; shown so the mass balance closes. Low/high: +-10% placeholder, one datum.

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: Mount Weld ore to Lynas WLP residue. Ore 0.075% ThO2 at 17-18% REO = 4.3 kg ThO2 per t REO = 1.5e7 Bq Th-232 (all Th reports to tailings or WLP). Bounds from ore grade ranges (max 0.18% ThO2; max 42% REO). Cross-check: concentrate 40% REO at 6.1 Bq/g gives 1.5e7. Measured WLP residue 6.2 Bq/g (up to 7.9) Th-232, about 75 000 t/a: 6.2e9 Bq per t residue. Concentrate tailings at the mine 1.8 Bq/g (177 kt/a). Malaysian WLP is classed radioactive (>1 Bq/g). Split between mine tailings (Australia) and WLP/NUF (Malaysia) not sourced: assume WLP takes the concentrate share.

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: Ionic (ion-adsorption) clays: ThO2 and U3O8 each about 0.005%, REO 0.05-1% (central 0.2%): 25 kg ThO2 per t REO = 8.9e7 Bq at 100% recovery; 1% REO gives 1.8e7, 0.05% gives 3.6e8. Selective leach leaves Th in the leached ore (soil-like, below 1 Bq/g, about 0.18 Bq/g), so concentrations are low but tonnages per t REO are large (about 500-2000 t). In-situ and heap leaching may leave the ore in place (is it a residue under D21?). Myanmar: no radiological data found. Southern China figure applies as a proxy.

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: Monazite route (Brazil/India/US/Malaysia/Australia). Monazite 4-12% Th and 50-68% REO (S0429): 0.059-0.24 t Th per t REO x 4.057e9 Bq/t Th = 2.4e8-9.8e8; central about 5e8 (8% Th at 58% REO). Th (99.3-99.99%) and 30-40% of Ra go to the hydroxide cake (22-28% Th oxide; about 2% of monazite mass in Brazil), and most remaining Ra to BaSO4 cake (6-10% of monazite mass). Source gives Th, not an activity: conversion is mine. Substantial historical dispersed use (cakes stored in drums, trenches).

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: Generic copper tailings. Ore handled 100-500 t per t Cu (EPA: several hundred; grade fell from about 1% to about 0.5% over the period). Activity 30-80 Bq/kg U-238 in US copper ore (UNSCEAR 1988 Table 46, S0008) up to 0.37 Bq/g for large-volume metal wastes (US EPA via IAEA TRS 419 Table XX, S0202). Low = 100 t x 30 Bq/kg; high = 500 t x 0.37 Bq/g; central is the geometric mean (judgement). Porphyry-type deposits only; copper-uranium deposits are in the Olympic Dam row.

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: As above with Th-232: ore 23-110 Bq/kg (Table 46), large-volume metal wastes 0.37 Bq/g (TRS 419 Table XX). Most Th stays in tailings (UNSCEAR 1988 notes concentrate Th is low).

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: Ra-226 0.19 Bq/g for large-volume metal wastes (TRS 419 Table XX) x 200-500 t ore; central at 200 t. Low bound (3.8e6) is a factor-10 judgement placeholder: no lower Ra-226 value was sourced.

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: Pb-210 0.13 Bq/g (TRS 419 Table XX) x 200 t = 2.6e7; high = 500 t; low is a factor-10 judgement bound. Po-210 is equal in Table XX (0.13): same numbers, group Po210.

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: As Pb210+ row (Table XX gives Pb-210 and Po-210 both 0.13 Bq/g).

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: Olympic Dam (Cu-U-Au-Ag). Ore milled 10.8 Mt / 212.5 kt Cu (FY2023) = 50.8 t ore per t Cu; Ra-226 in process feed 6.8-8.2 Bq/g (1994-95; 15 Bq/g in 1989 and 1993) gives 3.5e8-4.2e8; the high bound uses 15 Bq/g (1989-93 feed, 7.6e8). All Ra-226 is assumed to report to tailings. This is BEFORE co-product allocation: Cu about 74%, Au 13%, U 12%, Ag 1% by value in FY2023 (indicative). 4-10x the generic copper row. Consistency check: ore U 690 ppm = 8.5 Bq/g U-238; feed 9.2e13 Bq/a vs product 3.6e13 Bq (3406 t U3O8): about 39% of the U goes to product.

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: UNSCEAR 1988 Annex A Table 47 (page image, read by eye): one reference US copper smelter releases 7000 MBq/a Pb-210 and 7000 MBq/a Po-210 to air (also Th-232, Ra-228, Th-228 500 MBq/a, Th-230 700, U-238 and U-234 400, Ra-226 60). Capacity is NOT stated in the source: 100-300 kt Cu/a assumed (centre 173 kt) = 2.3e4-7e4 Bq per t Cu. Year of data about 1980-1985 (mid-1980s US plant). Modern capture lower; Po-210 volatilisation confirmed qualitatively in S0424.

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: As previous row (Po-210 7000 MBq/a).

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: Red mud per t Al = 1.7 t per t alumina (S0409) x 1.89 t alumina per t Al (stoichiometric Al2O3/2Al; my derivation) = 3.2 t. Th-232 in red mud 100-550 Bq/kg (compiled range 87-1350, S0409 Table 2; UNSCEAR 1988 180 Bq/kg US; central 400); broad TRS 419 range 100-3000 Bq/kg (S0202) would give up to 9.6e6. Residue enrichment about 1.1-1.6x bauxite (70% of Th and Ra to red mud).

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: Ra-226 100-1000 Bq/kg (S0409 Table 2: 13-1047), central 300, x 3.2 t red mud per t Al.

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: U-238 100-600 Bq/kg, central 280 (UNSCEAR 1988 Table 44 US plant) x 3.2 t/t. Red mud is also reused (bricks, soil conditioner, S0404 Table 3 list): Dispersed share not quantified.

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: UNSCEAR 2000 Annex B Table 28 (typical installation, 7500 kt/a ore throughput): airborne Pb-210 55 GBq/a, Po-210 90 GBq/a, Rn-222 180 GBq/a = 7.3e3, 1.2e4 and 2.4e4 Bq per t ore; x 1.4 t ore per t crude steel (S0421, BF-BOF) = 1.0e4 Pb-210 and 1.7e4 Po-210 per t steel. Low/high +-50% judgement. Applies to the integrated route only (EAF: scrap, little ore). Sinter-plant recycling of dust concentrates Pb/Po (S0202 section 6.4).

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: As previous row.

unit: Bq/t (head activity per tonne of refined commodity; REE per tonne REO; before co-product allocation; METHODS 3.2 multiplier NOT applied)
derivation_and_caveats: UNSCEAR 2000 Table 28: cement industry, 2000 kt/a throughput, airborne Po-210 78 GBq/a, Rn-222 157 GBq/a, Pb-210 0.2 GBq/a = 3.9e4 Bq Po-210 per t throughput. Raw meal per t cement about 1.5 t is assumed in the bounds (low = divide by 2, high = x2; judgement). Po-210 here probably comes largely from the kiln fuel (coal, petcoke): own and embedded parts cannot be separated from the table. Cement product itself 0.05-0.11 kBq/kg U-series, 0.03-0.1 Th-series (Table 27).

unit: Bq/t (head activity in the coal consumed; partition into ash, slag and stack by Task 1.3 factors)
derivation_and_caveats: Driver, not a residue activity: 0.8 t coal per t crude steel (BF-BOF, S0421) x coal 10-25 Bq/kg U-238 head (UNSCEAR 2000 Table 27 coal 0.01-0.025 kBq/kg; same for Th-232). Replace with the Task 1.3 coal factors per tonne coal (S0200-S0254) for the final value. The coke-oven and blast-furnace partitions are in Task 1.3.
